version.description:
Make a little progress, every day. Day in Ink gives your daily habits a simple place to live, with colorful cards, quick check-ins, and clear trends.

- Track numeric goals such as steps, minutes, or glasses of water.
- Add progress with a tap or enter an exact daily total.
- Track pass/fail habits with your choice of passed or failed as the daily default.
- Put important habits first with drag-and-drop ordering.
- Switch a habit between numeric progress and pass/fail while preserving earlier history.
- Review previous days and correct your history.
- Explore 7-, 30-, and 90-day trends, completion rates, and streaks.
- Archive habits while keeping their history.
- Export a backup and import it to restore habits and history.

Your habits stay in the app's storage on your iPhone. No account, ads, or analytics. App data may be included in your device backups. Exported backups are not encrypted by the app.

Support: https://apps.droessmj.com/day-in-ink/support.html
Privacy policy: https://apps.droessmj.com/day-in-ink/privacy.html

app_privacy.basis: The native app stores and processes habit data on-device, with no analytics SDK or developer-operated network service. User-selected exported files and Apple device backups are separately controlled. Support/privacy pages do not initialize analytics; the marketing home page uses Google Analytics as disclosed in the policy. The native app does not embed the website. Confirm this remains true for the final uploaded build.

app_review.notes: No account or sign-in is required. A fresh installation starts with Walk (10,000 steps), Drink Water (8 glasses), and Workout (pass/fail), with no fabricated check-in history. Tap + on Walk twice, wait for progress to update, relaunch, and verify persistence. Create a numeric habit with goal 1 and quick-add 0.1; ten additions complete it. Small nonzero amounts remain visible. Drag a habit's handle onto another habit on Today or Habits; verify the order in Trends and after relaunch. Move up/down menu and accessibility actions are also available. Open a pass/fail habit and test Passed, Failed, and Clear this day. Changing its Daily default affects unrecorded days, including past days; explicit check-ins remain unchanged. After logging today, change tracking type and Save: Cancel keeps the settings and log unchanged; confirming clears only today's incompatible log and applies the new settings. Earlier recorded days keep their original type, goal, unit, and result. In Habits > About > Export and import, export a backup, modify progress, import it, review it, and confirm replacement. Cancellation and rejected files leave existing data unchanged. Only current version 3 backups are accepted; no in-app older-format conversion exists. Gregorian start/day keys remain stable across timezone and calendar changes. Help & Support and Privacy Policy are accessible in About and recovery.

testflight.what_to_test: Persistent drag-and-drop and move-up/down ordering across Today, Habits, Trends and relaunches; tracking-type change confirmation, cancellation, both transition directions and earlier-history preservation; decimal quick-add completion and small numeric display; localized numeric entry; pass/fail defaults and overrides; export/import, cancellation and restore; rejection of unsupported backups without replacing data; history across timezone/calendar changes and clock rollback; rapid queued edits; support/privacy links; VoiceOver and maximum text size.

version.description:
Filter unwanted texts with keywords you choose. Blotter checks eligible messages from unknown senders on your iPhone and sends keyword matches to Junk.

- Add keywords or phrases to your own filtering rules.
- Choose case-sensitive, accent-sensitive, or whole-word matching.
- Process messages on your iPhone without sending message text to a developer-operated server.

Enable Blotter in iPhone Settings before using it. Filtering applies only to messages iOS provides to third-party text filters; iMessage and messages from Contacts are excluded. Matching is based on your chosen text rules, so broad keywords can also match legitimate messages.

Blotter does not keep a message or keyword-match history. No account, ads, or analytics SDK is required.

Support: https://apps.droessmj.com/blotter/support.html
Privacy policy: https://apps.droessmj.com/blotter/privacy.html

app_privacy.basis: The native app and embedded filter process message bodies and rules on-device without sending them off-device or recording match history. No legacy data or Keychain cleanup runs. Support/privacy pages do not initialize analytics; the marketing home page uses Google Analytics as disclosed separately. The native app does not embed the website. Confirm the final app and extension privacy reports and all SDKs.

app_review.notes: No account or sign-in is required. This app embeds the IdentityLookup message filter com.droessmj.blotter.filter; the extension does not have a separate store listing. In iPhone Settings > Apps > Messages, find text-message filtering and select Blotter. Onboarding acknowledgment does not verify activation; enablement instructions remain on Keywords. Add pineapple with default whole-word matching. From an unknown sender not in Contacts, send an eligible SMS containing pineapple offer; it should be classified as Junk. A message containing hello there should receive no classification from Blotter. Do not use iMessage for this test. iOS controls message eligibility. No message/match history exists. Help & Support and Privacy Policy links are accessible during setup and on Keywords. Rules and options use only group.com.droessmj.blotter; there is no old-state migration or Keychain entitlement.

testflight.what_to_test: Fresh onboarding and selecting Blotter in Messages settings; eligible unknown-sender SMS/MMS matches and nonmatches; case/accent/whole-word settings; rule edits reaching the extension; Contacts/iMessage exclusions; locked-device behavior after first unlock; rules/options persisting after relaunch; support/privacy links and maximum text size.

capabilities.identity_note: Current Blotter app and extension share only their own App Group. No prior app state or filter selection is migrated. No shared Keychain access is required.
